# Where the cycle was red-green and where it was not

Two slices were a real cycle. The providers slice recorded a RED (sequence 5) that
failed because `packages/providers` held tests and no implementation, then a GREEN
(sequence 6). The api slice recorded a RED (sequence 8) on a missing mailer and a
missing route, then a GREEN (sequence 9).

`packages/providers/src/stack.test.ts` was not. Those six tests exercise the storage
and telemetry implementations against real Supabase and a real collector, and they
were written after the implementations they cover, so they passed the first time they
ran. They are regression cover for code the providers slice wrote, not a cycle, and
calling them a RED would be a false claim about how they came about.

The judgement behind that: what was new at that point was the environment, not the
code. The implementations had landed in the providers slice with the containers still
to exist, and once the containers existed the honest thing was to find out whether the
code worked against them. It did. Had it not, the failure would have been a defect
found late rather than a RED, which is exactly the cost of writing them in that order
and is worth naming rather than dressing up.

The environment itself carries no unit tests at all and is not meant to: a compose
file, a `config.toml`, four shell scripts and a workflow are proven by being run, and
those runs are recorded at sequence 10.
